subject: using a computer, phone or internet to learn, and what gets in the way
citation: Challenges of e-learning adoption in South African public schools: learners' perspectives (Journal of Education and e-Learning Research)
Evaluation of e-learning usage in South African universities (ERIC)
A user experience evaluation of the Siyavula software for mathematics education for learners with special education needs (CPUT dissertation)

claims.text: Device and data costs can block online learning in low-income households, even when learners see educational value.
objections: Will this add to the financial burden my household already carries?

claims.text: A noisy or crowded home can make online learning feel less effective than contact classes.
objections: Do I have a quiet, private space to use this properly?

claims.text: Some learners may value interactive tools with quick feedback and visual content, though interest does not guarantee sustained use.
Slow internet and computer shortages can frustrate learners before they engage with the content.
objections: Will this even work on our slow internet and shared computers?

confidence: Multi-source qualitative synthesis combining learner surveys, instructor interviews, and literature reviews across South African schools and universities — mechanisms are robustly triangulated, but magnitudes and precise regional variation are unknown.
